protocol_blocked_summary.finding: The Codex CLI app-server client at packages/happy-cli/src/codex/codexAppServerClient.ts:280-364 emits ONLY 3 EventMsg item types — commandExecution, fileChange, agentMessage. Line 364 silently consumes all other item types via `return method.startsWith('item/')`. EventMsg is a loose `{type: string} & Record<string, unknown>` with no discriminated union for any additional verbs.
protocol_blocked_summary.impact: This protocol gap blocks live rendering for 14 of the 17 Codex tools Cycle 1 was designed to cover: 7 of 9 Phase B tools (write_stdin, update_plan, request_user_input, list_mcp_resources, list_mcp_resource_templates, read_mcp_resource, view_image), all 5 Phase C verbs (spawn_agent, send_input, wait_agent, resume_agent, close_agent), both Phase D tools (tool_suggest, multi_tool_use.parallel). Only 3 tools in Cycle 1 scope are NOT protocol-blocked — apply_patch (already mapped via patch_apply_begin/end), mcp__happy__change_title (a Claude wire-name alias, not a Codex tool), and the §5.4 cleanup (not a Codex tool at all).
protocol_blocked_summary.cycle_1_mitigation: DORMANT RENDERER strategy adopted. UI surface shipped complete: knownTools entries + toolViewRegistry entries + view components + i18n keys + TODO comments in sessionProtocolMapper.ts documenting activation patterns that mirror the existing exec_command_begin/end template (lines 294-322). When the Codex protocol is extended in a future cycle to emit these events, only sessionProtocolMapper.ts needs new branches — no happy-app changes required.

This single architectural change would activate ALL 14 dormant renderers simultaneously — extremely high leverage per unit of effort.

unresolved_issues.description: §5.10 — Long background-task disconnect causes out-of-order delivery on reconnect. Multi-package transport bug (happy-app messageQueue + happy-cli apiSession + happy-server sessionRoutes). Needs dedicated cycle.
unresolved_issues.last_attempt_reason: Cycle 1 deferred by PM TRIAGE plan — multi-package transport bug cannot be bundled with UI work; spec Section 8 explicitly states '§5.10 is ALONE'
unresolved_issues.recommended_approach: Dedicated cycle. Step 1: BA writes reproducible repro harness (long bash background task `sleep 300 && echo done &` + simulated WebSocket disconnect via chrome://net-internals or Cloudflare drop) — commit the harness first, before any implementation. Step 2: Dev implements proactive reconnect in apiSession.ts heartbeat loop (reconnect when 2 consecutive intervals miss, do NOT wait for next user message). Step 3: Dev implements causal ordering — server assigns monotonic per-session sequence to every message; client maintains reorder buffer keyed by sequence. Step 4: Verify with repro: user message reply arrives BEFORE background-task self-reply on reconnect. MANDATORY: daemon rebuild + restart before QA (cycle-1 lesson from §5.9).

patterns_noticed: DORMANT RENDERER strategy worked exactly as designed — UI surface shipped complete, protocol extension deferred to dedicated cycle. Pattern is now proven and should be the default approach for any multi-layer feature where one layer is protocol-blocked.

BA-QA mid-pipeline gate caught architecture errors before Dev started: pipeline 0 FAIL on iter1 (8 objections, ill-specified) → PASS on iter2 after BA tightened spec. Pipeline 1 FAIL on iter1 (4 objections) → PASS on iter2. Cost of BA-QA iteration is a small fraction of wasted Dev iteration. Gate must be preserved.

Protocol-first inspection is a new pattern — BA now explicitly inspects the CLI protocol layer BEFORE writing the UI spec. Pipelines 0, 1, 2 all adopted this pattern and correctly identified the protocol-block. This should be codified in BA's agent prompt as a mandatory step for any Codex tool feature.

Live-evidence gap remains a structural limit — 4 of 4 pipelines hit a source+bundle fallback for at least one acceptance criterion. This is the cumulative cost of no Codex session in dev. A single user action (manual Codex session provisioning) would eliminate the gap for ALL future Codex cycles.

Shared-primitive amortization continues to pay off: Phase C used ONE shared CodexSubagentView (66 LOC) for 5 verbs. Phase B's apply_patch reused existing CodexPatchView (no new view file). Pattern is now canonical for Codex phased rollouts.
